subtype: Blank expression in exhaustion or burnout [Interpreting]
passage: Sun, 9:40 pm. Tanuja has looked blank for three weeks. At the stand-up she stares at the wall, answers in one word, no smile. I nearly told my manager she seems checked out. Then today I saw her in the pantry, holding a cup of tea and not drinking it, just standing. She looked so tired. I said, "Want to walk to the gate for some air?" and she came. She said the release plus her father's hospital visits has left her flat. I offered to take over the test report for a week. She teared up a little and thanked me. I am glad I did not judge her attitude. I am Nikita, by the way, and I feel a bit guilty for the thoughts I had earlier. 🙂

qa.q: What did Nikita offer to do for Tanuja?
qa.a: She offered to take over the test report for a week.

qa.q: Why did Nikita change her mind about Tanuja seeming checked out?
qa.a: She saw Tanuja standing in the pantry, tired and not drinking her tea, and then learned about the release and her father's hospital visits. The blank face turned out to mean exhaustion, though before that it could have meant boredom.

qa.q: What did Nikita do that helped Tanuja?
qa.a: She offered a walk in private and practical help with the report instead of reporting Tanuja to a manager.

qa.q: How might Tanuja have felt when Nikita invited her to the gate?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and slightly emotional to be noticed kindly, since she teared up when she got practical help.

grounding: Diary entry of a colleague who reads a weeks-long blank face as possible exhaustion and offers private check-in and practical help.

passage:
Arohi: Kamal, you okay? You have been very quiet in meetings lately
Kamal: I am fine
Arohi: You do not have to say more. Your face has been kind of blank for a while. I thought maybe you are drained
Kamal: Kind of. Two projects and the audit
Arohi: That is a lot. Want me to take the vendor calls this week?
Kamal: Would you? That would help a lot 🙏
Arohi: Sure. And no pressure to talk, just tell me if you need anything else
Kamal: Thanks. I honestly thought people believed I did not care
Arohi: I did not, I just wanted to check 🙂

qa.q: What did Arohi offer to take over for Kamal?
qa.a: Arohi offered to take the vendor calls this week.

qa.q: What does Kamal's line about people believing Kamal did not care suggest about the feeling?
qa.a: It suggests Kamal felt worn down and worried about being misjudged. The short answers could also have hidden something more than workload, but two projects and the audit were named.

qa.q: What did Arohi do well in this chat?
qa.a: Arohi checked in privately, did not push Kamal to explain, and gave practical help with the vendor calls.

qa.q: How might Kamal have felt reading Arohi's first message?
qa.a: Kamal might have felt exposed or defensive at first, given the reply "I am fine", but then relieved that help was offered and not criticism.

grounding: Chat in which a colleague reads a blank face as possible overload and offers a private check-in and practical help.
